pulls.title: Prefer URI values; forbid automated decisions based on the value
pulls.author: jdevalk
pulls.body:
Implements the two changes proposed in reply to Asbjorn Ulsberg's review of the draft:

1. The value SHOULD be a URI identifying the redirect decision-maker (e.g. its home page), to avoid collisions between components that share a name and remove ambiguity. Added a URI example in the Syntax section.
2. States explicitly that the field is for human diagnosis of redirects and that recipients MUST NOT base automated decisions on the value, with an example of the forbidden pattern (following or ignoring a redirect depending on whether the value matches a particular identifier).

pulls.title: Adopt Rory Hewitt's review feedback: String-only values and diagnostic context
pulls.author: jdevalk
pulls.body:
Addresses Rory Hewitt's review on the list (19 Oct 2026):

1. **String-only values.** The value MUST now be a String, never a Token. A single serialization supports both the recommended URI prefix and optional human-readable diagnostic context while keeping parsing simple. Migration from X-Redirect-By already requires a new field name, so quoting is trivial.

2. **Diagnostic context after the URI.** The String SHOULD begin with a URI identifying the kind of component, avoiding collisions. It MAY continue with opaque, human-readable context that helps an operator identify the installation, deployment, handler, function, plugin, or rule that issued the redirect, for example: `Redirect-By: "https://wordpress.org/; FrontEndBypass"`. The document defines no structure for this context and requires recipients to treat the entire String as opaque.

Rory's third point (the "redirect decision-maker" editorial nit) was already addressed in merged PR #1; no change was needed here.
